name: arm-robot-pour
_: The whole machine: a SHOULDER carrying a WRIST carrying a GRIPPER, each one a real sub-assembly. Seven axes — j1…j5 on the arm, grip and roll in the tool. The gripper arrives whole from ../gripper in its embedded mode, and it brings a finding with it: ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 puts four M6 on a Ø50 circle, r 25, and the gripper's NEMA 17 sits on the back of its own web at 42.3 square — half-diagonal 29.9. The standard's bolt circle falls INSIDE the motor, so the two cannot be bolted face to face. The tool adapter is a cup that reaches back past the motor and picks up the web's r 48.5 circle instead: 54 mm of extra tool length and 360 g at the very tip, which is the worst place on the machine to spend either.

base-plate._: Bench plate: Ø182 × 12, four M8 on a Ø144 circle into the bench. The whole machine's overturning moment lands here — 73 N·m of it with the arm out and the counterweights swung — so it is bolted down, not weighted down. One extrude along +Z.

column._: Column: Ø84 over Ø60, z 12…240. Hollow because the J1 harmonic's cabling and the whole arm's CAN bus run up the middle — a cable bundle outside a rotating joint is the thing that fails first. One extrude along +Z.

joint-small._: Actuator module stand-in, Ø50 × 45: the wrist's three. They see inertia and a little friction, nothing else — the tool's weight is reacted at the wrist centre, not by these.

can._: A 330 ml can, Ø66 × 123. Reference geometry — it is the task, not the machine.

pin._: Ø12 ground dowel through a parallelogram joint. One extrude along -Y.

assembly._: the shoulder — pedestal, parallelogram and forearm

turret._: J1 output plate: Ø92 × 14 on top of the column, carrying both shoulder cheeks. One extrude along +Z.

cheek._: Shoulder cheek, two off at |y| 62…74: they straddle the whole parallelogram and carry the COAXIAL J2 and J3 bores at z 400. Coaxial is the architecture — it is what puts the elbow's actuator at the shoulder and lets one counterweight per crank balance the arm exactly. `y1` is overridden per side. One extrude along -Y.

joint-large._: Actuator module stand-in, Ø80 × 70: NEMA 17 plus a 20:1 reduction, used at J2 and J3. Drawn along -Y; J1's instance is turned onto Z. The balanced J2 and J3 need 1.9 N·m against the 6.2 this delivers.

upper-arm._: Upper arm, J2 to the elbow, 250 mm, with a 300 mm rear extension carrying CW1. 60 × 20 on the centre plane. One extrude along -Y.

counterweight._: Counterweight: a plain steel cylinder Ø70 on a link's rear extension. CW1 is 2.55 kg (× 42.3 long) on the upper arm and CW2 4.07 kg (× 40.8) on the J3 cranks. Length is overridden per instance — the mass IS the tuning, and it is shimmable with washers. One extrude along -Y.

crank._: J3 crank, two off, coaxial with J2 and 80 mm long: the push rod hangs off its front end and CW2 off its 200 mm rear extension. The push rod delivers the forearm's whole gravitational moment here 1:1, which is exactly why a counterweight at this radius balances it at every angle. One extrude along -Y.

push-rod._: Push rod, two off, 250 mm — the same length as the upper arm and always parallel to it. That is the parallelogram: it makes the elbow crank parallel to the J3 crank, so the FOREARM'S ABSOLUTE ANGLE IS j3, whatever j2 does. One extrude along -Y.

elbow-crank._: Elbow crank, two off, 80 mm — the parallelogram's fourth bar, rigid with the forearm and reaching from its side face out under the push rod. One extrude along -Y.

forearm._: Forearm, elbow to the J4 roll section, 180 mm of a 250 mm reach. It carries no actuator: j3 arrives through the elbow crank from the shoulder. One extrude along -Y.

forearm-barrel._: Forearm barrel: Ø64 over Ø56, 80 long, swallowing the J4 motor and its reduction. The two forearm plates land on this instead of ending in mid-air. Ø64 and not Ø54 because a NEMA 17's DIAGONAL is 59.8. One extrude along +X.

nema17._: NEMA 17 stand-in: 42.3 square with 5 mm corner chamfers, 40 long. Two off — J4 coaxial up the forearm, J5 crosswise in the roll drum. One extrude along +X.

planetary._: Planetary reduction stand-in, Ø42 × 32. J4 takes 30:1 for its 5.57 N·m corner case; J5 takes only 10:1 because the belt is the other 3:1 — which is why the belt makes the gearbox cheaper, not dearer. One extrude along +X.

roll-bearing._: J4 bearing: Ø80 over Ø64, between the fixed barrel and the turning drum. It carries the whole wrist's cantilever — 5.6 N·m of it — so it is a crossed roller, like the gripper's. One extrude along +X.

assembly._: j4: the drum, the J5 drive inside it, the fork and the belt

roll-drum._: J4 roll drum: Ø118 over Ø110, turning with j4 and carrying the fork. It is this big because the J5 motor lies CROSSWISE inside it — that is the whole trick, and it is what takes the wrist's swept circle from Ø271 down to Ø118. The belt leaves through its open front face. One extrude along +X.

nema17._: NEMA 17 stand-in: 42.3 square with 5 mm corner chamfers, 40 long. Two off — J4 coaxial up the forearm, J5 crosswise in the roll drum. One extrude along +X.

planetary._: Planetary reduction stand-in, Ø42 × 32. J4 takes 30:1 for its 5.57 N·m corner case; J5 takes only 10:1 because the belt is the other 3:1 — which is why the belt makes the gearbox cheaper, not dearer. One extrude along +X.

pulley._: GT2 pulley at its PITCH diameter, drawn at ROOT diameter so the belt band clears it — the teeth we do not draw are what fills the 0.8 mm between them. Two off: 20T Ø12.73 on the J5 gearbox and 60T Ø38.2 on the pitch shaft. One extrude along -Y.

belt._: GT2 9 belt, 20T to 60T over 85 mm of centres — drawn as a real band so its envelope is a real clearance body, which the blade and the cheek both have to miss. One extrude along -Y.

fork-cheek._: J5 fork cheek, two off at |y| 27…39: carries the pitch bush at the wrist centre. `y1` is overridden per side. One extrude along -Y.

fork-web._: J5 fork web: the 54 mm spacer the two cheeks bolt to, closing the back of the slot and taking the roll tube's face. One extrude along -Y.

pitch-bush._: Flanged bush in a fork cheek, Ø22 outside on Ø16. Two off. One extrude along -Y.

assembly._: j5: the blade, its shaft, the driven pulley and the flange

wrist-blade._: J5 blade: the tool-side member, 50 thick between the fork's cheeks, bored on the pitch axis and flaring from x 45 to a 63 face for the tool flange. The flare starts where it does because everything on this part sweeps r = hypot(x, z) about the pitch axis, and inside r 43.01 it would find a fork cheek. One extrude along +Z, then the pitch bore as a cut along Y.

pitch-shaft._: Ø16 pitch shaft, pressed into the blade and running in a bush in each cheek. One extrude along -Y.

pulley._: GT2 pulley at its PITCH diameter, drawn at ROOT diameter so the belt band clears it — the teeth we do not draw are what fills the 0.8 mm between them. Two off: 20T Ø12.73 on the J5 gearbox and 60T Ø38.2 on the pitch shaft. One extrude along -Y.

tool-flange._: Tool flange, ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6: Ø63 × 8, four M6 on a Ø50 circle, Ø31.5 pilot. The gripper's own web bolts to this — its README calls this interface out and does not draw it, so this is the half that exists. One extrude along +X.

assembly._: the gripper — ../gripper v10, whole, with the adapter its own motor forces

motor-web._: Motor web — the only solid plate on the stator and the whole of its structure. The NEMA 17 hangs on its outside on the pilot and four M3; the screw passes through the middle; four M3 on a Ø97 circle carry the bearing housing, four Ø3 dowels at r 22 key the brake ring. It takes no grip load at all now: the grip runs pillar to rotor plate to bearing, and the bearing hands it to this plate as a moment. The tool interface belongs here; it is not drawn yet. One extrude along -Y.

bearing-housing._: Bearing housing: a Ø104 ring, 13 deep, bored Ø90 for the crossed-roller ring’s outer race and tapped four M3 for the guard. The race is a press fit and a retaining plate is not drawn. This ring and the web are the stator; everything ahead of the race turns. One extrude along -Y.

bearing._: Crossed-roller ring stand-in (THK RB6013 or equivalent): Ø60 bore × Ø90 × 13, drawn as one annulus because the races and the rollers are the vendor’s problem. It IS the roll axis, and it is chosen for MOMENT: the grip puts 61 N at a fingertip 114 mm ahead of it, 7.0 N·m, and a crossed roller takes that alone where a deep-groove pair would want 30 mm of spacing this module has nowhere to put. One extrude along -Y.

shroud._: Guard: a Ø104 × 3 tube from the bearing housing to 1 mm short of the turning rail plate. It carries nothing — the pillars carry the grip and the bearing carries the moment — so it is printed, and its bore clears the arms’ Ø81 sweep by 11 mm a side. One extrude along -Y.

rotor-plate._: Rotor plate: a Ø84 disc on the bearing’s inner race, four M3 on a Ø68 circle. Both pillars thread M8 into it and their Ø10 shoulders bear on its front face, so the grip tension arrives here and goes straight into the race. Ø12 in the middle clears the screw; the nut never comes back this far. This is the root of the rotating group. One extrude along -Y.

front-wall._: Rail plate — the front of the rotating group. A Ø100 disc: the strip across its middle carries the MGN9 rail on its OUTER face, tapped M3 at the rail’s own 20 mm pitch, and the screw’s Ø6.2 journal runs in a blind bore at its centre, closed by the rail itself. Either side of the strip a long slot lets a coupling link pass through, over and under the rail. Two M8 tapped holes at x ±24 take the pillars, drawn at the tap drill and blind because the rail closes them off. Nothing bolts to a case any more: the case does not turn and this does. One extrude along -Y.

motor._: NEMA 17 external linear stepper body (42.3 square, 5 mm corner chamfers, 48 mm stack) with an integrated Tr8×2 lead screw as its shaft — the shortest catalogue stack that carries a 2 mm lead (the screw is its own tree). Sits behind the bulkhead. One extrude along -Y.

brake-spring._: Brake spring: a wave washer, drawn as the flat annulus it becomes when compressed. It is the whole adjustment — its preload times the friction radius is the torque the rotor is held by, and that torque is what the grip breaks away at. 18.6 N for 0.112 N·m, which is a light washer. One extrude along -Y.

brake-ring._: Brake ring: the friction face, keyed to the motor web by four Ø3 dowels so it cannot turn, and pushed onto the rotor’s hub by the wave washer behind it. Bronze or a filled PTFE — μ 0.3 is assumed and it is the one number here a bench would settle. One extrude along -Y.

brake-hub._: Brake hub: the rotor’s half of the brake, a Ø58 disc inside the bearing’s bore, bolted to the back of the rotor plate. The screw runs through its Ø12 bore. Everything the rotor is held by passes through this face, so the grip force is set here and not in software. One extrude along -Y.

encoder-ring._: Encoder ring: a multipole magnet pressed onto the rotor plate’s rim, read radially. The axis is taken by the screw, so an on-axis diametric magnet is not available and this is the way round it. One extrude along -Y.

encoder-head._: Encoder head: the sensor and its bracket in one, bolted to the bearing housing’s front face and reaching forward past the rotor plate to read the ring across a 1 mm gap. It lives in the 4 mm of radial slot between the ring and the guard, which is the only stationary place left at this diameter. One extrude along -Y.

nut._: Tr8 flange nut stand-in: 22 mm flange, 10 mm body, 8.4 mm bore (thread not modelled; the 0.2 mm is the thread clearance). The flange sits behind the carriage, so gripping loads it in compression. One revolve about local Z.

carriage-back._: Carriage back plate, 4 thick: the thrust plate. The nut’s flange bolts to its rear face and the pivot arms bottom on its front face, so gripping runs nut → plate → arm as pure compression through one Y-normal joint — no bolt sees the thrust. One extrude along -Y.

carriage._: Nut carriage, 10 thick: the key plate. Its outline is notched open to each side (from x ±9 to the edge, 22.2 tall) and a pivot arm drops into each notch from outside, so the arm is located in X and Z and held square, while its thrust goes straight back into the back plate. Open notches, not closed slots — a closed slot cannot be assembled around an arm that reaches past it. The four bolts through the nut flange carry on through both plates. One extrude along -Y.

arm._: Pivot arm: a 22 mm block on the grip plane, dropped into the carriage key plate’s open notch and bottomed on the back plate, carrying the link pivot pin at x 34 with a link seated on each of its faces. Bored Ø10.2 at x 24 for its pillar: the arm slides on it, and that is what holds the plunger square and stops it turning. Two per gripper (side = 1 right, -1 left); a set screw holds it in the carriage (not modelled). Local origin at the carriage centre. One extrude along +Z, then the pillar bore as a cut along Y.

link._: Link: a 43 mm dog-bone, 6 thick, with two Ø6 eyes for pressed bronze bushings. Four per gripper: one above and one below, at z ±11…17, clear of the blocks. From the arm pin, through a slot in the front wall, to the jaw carrier’s pin outside. Built along +X from eye 0; the assembly rotates it about Z. One extrude.

bushing._: Bronze bushing: Ø6 × 6 with a Ø4.1 bore, pressed into a link eye, running on a Ø4 dowel. Eight per gripper. One revolve about local Z.

pin._: A 4 mm hardened dowel, 34 long, along +Z: pressed through a pivot arm or a jaw carrier, carrying a link above and a link below in bronze bushings (retaining clips not modelled). Four per gripper. One extrude.

carrier._: Jaw plate: 32 × 22 × 8, bolted to the outer face of its MGN9C block (four M3 on the block’s 10 × 15 pattern). The Ø4 link pin passes through it along Z with 22 mm of bearing, 10.5 mm inboard of its centre and 5.5 from its inner edge, so the pin sits close to the grip line and the two plates meet on the centre line at closed — that meeting is the stop. Outboard of the pin, the finger mount: four M4 and two Ø5 dowels in two columns, tapped through and closed off by the block behind, so a finger bolt is 8 mm at most. The pin hole is a cut along Z, the only boolean in this design. One extrude along +Y.

pillar._: Pillar: the frame’s primary member. A Ø10 body between the two plates of the ROTOR, with an M8 end at each: into the rotor plate behind and the rail plate ahead. Grip pulls the rail plate forward and the rotor plate back, so both threads are in tension and the Ø10 shoulders take the compression — and the whole of it, tension and moment, arrives at the crossed-roller ring, which is the only joint to the stator. It also pierces its pivot arm, so it is the plunger’s alignment rail and its anti-rotation. Two per gripper, on the grip plane at x ±24. Threads are modelled at their minor diameter (Ø6.65 for M8), which is a real 0.075 mm clear of the Ø6.8 tap drill — drawing both at the tap drill made two coincident cylinders and 0.72 mm³ of mesh flank. One revolve about local Z, placed along +Y.

block._: MGN9C linear block stand-in: 20 × 10 × 28.9, wrapping the rail with a 10 × 5 channel, its base 2 mm off the wall. Its four M3 face +Y, into the jaw carrier. One extrude along +X.

rail._: MGN9 rail stand-in: 9 × 6.5 section, 104 long, on the OUTER face of the front wall’s strip, centred on z = 0, closing the screw’s journal bore behind it (its own counterbores are not modelled; the wall’s tapped holes are). One extrude along +X.

tool-adapter._: Tool adapter: the cup that bolts ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 on the arm to the gripper's Ø104 web on its r 48.5 circle, reaching back past the motor's end because the standard's own bolt circle (r 25) falls inside a 42.3 square motor (half-diagonal 29.9). The two CANNOT be bolted face to face; this part is what that costs. One revolve about the tool axis.

assembly._: The lead screw, on the STATOR — it is axisymmetric, so rolling it changes no geometry. What rolling changes is the GRIP, by the lead, and in this machine that is a feature rather than a fault: rolling only happens once the nut has stopped, and then the screw and the rotor turn together and the nut does not move at all. (v9’s thrust collar is gone with this: the motor carries the thrust on its own bearing, a Tr8 screw has nowhere smooth to clamp a collar, and it sat exactly where the brake stack now goes.)

screw._: Tr8×2 lead screw, the stepper’s own shaft: an 8 mm cylinder from the motor face, turned down to a Ø6 journal for the last 8 mm, which runs in the front wall’s blind bore; the thread is not modelled. One revolve about local Z, placed along +Y.
